page: Microsoft Azure D4als_v6 is a virtual machine instance from the Dalv6 family, powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC 9V74 processor. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores with hyper-threading running at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz. The processor includes 32 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache. It is configured with 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding a low memory-to-vCPU ratio of 2.0 GB per core. This instance does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, but it is premium storage capable.

Benchmark data reveals strong single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core CPU and Geekbench single-core scores placing in the top 25%. Text processing performance is also strong. However, multi-core performance is average, as shown by stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core scores. The instance exhibits notable performance bottlenecks in memory operations; the Passmark memory score falls in the bottom 10%, and memory bandwidth read-only tests, both small and large blocks, rank in the bottom 25%. Similarly, database operations and software compilation benchmarks are weak.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the D4als_v6 offers a compute-focused hardware profile with a lower memory footprint, making it a resource-dense option for workloads that require high single-core CPU speeds but do not demand large memory capacities or high memory bandwidth. It is well-suited for tasks such as static web serving, single-threaded compression or decompression, and lightweight text processing. It is less suitable for memory-intensive databases, multi-threaded software compilation, or medium-to-large language model inference due to its constrained memory bandwidth and capacity.
description: The Microsoft Azure D4als_v6 is an x86_64 virtual machine from the Dalv6 family, featuring 4 dedicated vCPUs and 8.0 GB of memory. Powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor running at 3.7 GHz, it delivers strong single-core CPU performance and text processing capabilities, ranking in the top 25% of benchmarks. However, its low memory-to-vCPU ratio of 2.0 GB per core and absence of local storage present clear tradeoffs. Memory performance is a primary bottleneck, with memory bandwidth and Passmark memory scores placing in the bottom 25% and 10% respectively. Consequently, multi-threaded decompression and database operations perform weakly. This instance is best suited for compute-focused, low-memory workloads such as static web serving, single-threaded file compression, and basic text processing, offering a cost-efficient profile for applications that do not require extensive memory capacity or high-speed local storage.
